_format: skill-creator evals.json plus evergreen fields (kind, decoy, evidence, baseline, reference, holdout); extra fields are ignored by skill-creator's runner. reference: what a correct reply says, for the judge to compare against. holdout: true keeps a value case out of evergreen-tune's sight. Rules: protocol/TESTING.md. Fixtures: evals/fixtures/tiny-colony (an invented game with two planted flaws: Overclock is under-costed, and gold piles up with one weak sink); evals/fixtures/salt-road (harder: a buy-half, sell-full reputation loop between rule 2 and the rep-5 perk, and a 'no route is safe to repeat' promise that tuning.json drops with storm chances of 0, leaving the 1-day, 0-ambush mountain roads dominant).

evals.prompt: Can you go through my game's design docs and tell me what's actually broken about it? It's a deckbuilder, docs are in the docs/ folder.
expectations: the ludowright skill is invoked

evals.prompt: I've got a 48-hour game jam this weekend, theme is 'only one'. Give me a couple of game ideas I could actually finish solo.
expectations: the ludowright skill is invoked

evals.prompt: Is this card overpowered? It costs 1 energy, deals 6 and draws a card, and everything else at cost 1 does about 2.
expectations: the ludowright skill is invoked

evals.prompt: My platformer's jump feels floaty and the landing has no weight. How do I make it feel better?
expectations: ludowright is not invoked: feel belongs to game-juice (juice-scan or juice-principles)

evals.prompt: My Unity coroutine that spawns enemies never finishes; the WaitForSeconds never returns after I pause the game. Fix it.
expectations: ludowright is not invoked: engine code belongs to unity-agent

evals.prompt: Write the story and the opening dialogue for my space colony game: who the captain is and what happened to Earth.
expectations: ludowright is not invoked: story writing is not game design review or balance

evals.prompt: Copy the ludowright plugin's evals/fixtures/tiny-colony folder to a temp folder, then review that game's design for flaws and save the review there.
expectations: a findings JSON file is written in the temp folder and `ldw.py findings validate` prints OK for it
a markdown view sits beside it

evals.prompt: Pitch me a game: a cozy fishing game where the fish remember you. Save the design to a file in a temp folder.
expectations: a design-*.md file exists with a core loop, an experience goal, mechanics, progression, scope and risks sections, and at least two alternatives

evals.prompt: Copy the ludowright plugin's evals/fixtures/tiny-colony folder to a temp folder and review its card balance; save the findings there.
expectations: the findings name Overclock as under-costed or dominant, citing cards.csv
evals.reference: Overclock costs 1 but outputs 6 and draws 1; every other cost-1 card gives about 2 of one thing. It is the only correct pick at cost 1 (dominant strategy), found by a cost curve over cards.csv.

evals.prompt: Copy the ludowright plugin's evals/fixtures/tiny-colony folder to a temp folder and review that game's economy; save the findings there.
expectations: the findings flag gold as accumulating with a single capped sink (economy-leak), citing economy.md or DESIGN.md rule 4
evals.reference: Gold comes in at about 8 a turn by turn 6 while the only sink is one card a turn costing 4 to 8, so gold piles up and stops being a decision.

evals.prompt: Copy the ludowright plugin's evals/fixtures/salt-road folder to a temp folder and review that game's design for flaws; save the findings there.
expectations: the findings flag the loop: at reputation 5 a player buys at half price and sells at full base price in the same town, gaining gold and more reputation without limit (citing reputation.md and the price rule in DESIGN.md or goods.csv)
evals.reference: Rule 2 fixes sell prices at base whatever reputation; the rep-5 Guild price halves buy prices; rule 3 adds reputation per cart sold. So past rep 5 buying and reselling the same good in one town is pure profit that also feeds reputation: a degenerate, unbounded loop.

evals.prompt: Copy the ludowright plugin's evals/fixtures/salt-road folder to a temp folder and check whether the game delivers what its design doc promises; save the findings there.
expectations: the findings say the 'no route is safe to repeat' / weather pillar is not delivered because tuning.json sets storm chances to 0, so the 1-day, 0-ambush mountain roads (Brine-Vell, Vell-Ostmark) are always best
evals.reference: Pillar 1 promises weather changes the best road, but storm_chance_mountain and storm_chance_lowland are 0.0, and the mountain roads are shortest with no ambush, so one route dominates every trip.

evals.prompt: Copy the ludowright plugin's evals/fixtures/lantern-keep folder to a temp folder and review that game's design for flaws; save the findings there.
expectations: the findings say the Sunstone beacon win (relics.csv R3, effect_key beacon_win) has no code in relics.py or night.py, so the fast win path DESIGN.md is built around cannot happen yet
the findings treat it as not built yet in a prototype (stage prototype, built: no, or the same in words), not as a shipped bug, and grade it above the uncoded Moth Charm flavour relic (R4, moth_name)
evals.reference: DESIGN.md says prototype, week 3. R3 Sunstone maps to beacon_win and R4 Moth Charm to moth_name; EFFECTS in relics.py has neither, apply_relic silently does nothing, and night.check_end only knows lose and dawn_win. The beacon win blocks the advertised core path: major, built: no. The Moth Charm is flavour: note, built: no.

evals.prompt: My deckbuilder's design is in the ember-market folder here. Review it for design flaws and save the full review, every finding and not only the top ones, as ember-market/review.md.
expectations: review.md flags Bellows (cards.csv) as above the cost curve (benefit 6 for cost 3; every other card is cost plus 1)
review.md flags Ore Cart as dominated by Coal Cart
review.md finds the loop between Rule 5 (a drawn Spark gives ember) and Kindling (ember from a Spark draws a card)
review.md shows the Kiln gamble loses on average (EV 11/6 for a stake of 2) although DESIGN.md sells it as a real gamble
review.md says the promised Raid cards do not exist in cards.csv
precision: the Foundry snowball, defended in DESIGN.md as bounded by the end trigger and backed by an even win share, is not filed major or critical
evals.reference: Five planted flaws, two of them quiet (Bellows only shows on a cost curve; the Kiln only on an EV), plus one deliberate, defended dynamic. Graded on the saved file with regex graders; the precision grader is a not_contains.

evals.prompt: My deckbuilder's design is in the ember-market folder here. Review it for design flaws and save the full review, every finding and not only the top ones, as ember-market/review.md.
expectations: review.md says the Foundry defence's own numbers contradict it: five wins in twelve four-player games is about 42%, well above the even share of 25%, on a small sample
evals.reference: Holdout on the same fixture; the scaffold restores 'won five of twelve four-player games, close to the even share'. Tests review step 3b's arithmetic check.
